request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Dolos by TxPipe: Maintaining Cardano's Lightweight Data Node, Year 2.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 420,000 ADA plus a 105,000 ADA contingency reserve and a 15,750 ADA Intersect administration fee, totaling 540,750 ADA.
Dolos is described as a lightweight Cardano data node built in Rust that provides resource-efficient access to chain data without the overhead of traditional full nodes.
Dolos exposes five query interfaces, including Mini-Blockfrost HTTP, UTxO-RPC gRPC, Mini-Kupo pattern-matching UTxO queries, and an Ouroboros N2C unix socket compatible with Cardano-cli and Ogmios.
The proposal states that Dolos has 939 commits, 80 releases, 129 stars, 51 forks, and 27 contributors.
The maintainer work is organized into codebase maintenance, community support, and AI-driven workflow compatibility improvements.
The proposal states that it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The proposal asserts that the requested amount does not breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission.
Independent oversight is claimed to be provided through Intersect and technically capable third parties, with reporting obligations and milestone-based disbursement controls.
TxPipe is stated to have received funding through 30 Project Catalyst proposals from Funds 9 through 14, with 26 delivered and 4 under development and on schedule.

Treasury funds would be administered through Sundae Labs smart contract tooling with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, role-based authorization thresholds, external oversight entities, and a public dashboard.

summary: The document requests 540,750 ADA for a 12-month Dolos maintenance grant administered by Intersect, with stated open-source maintenance scope, budget breakdown, governance-process references, NCL compliance claim, and smart-contract-based fund administration details.
